SFPUC Employee Retirement Recognitions for 25+ Years of Service
items.text: SFPUC Employee Retirement Recognitions for 25+ Years of Service General Manager Dennis Herrera recognized the incredible service and dedication of employees who would soon retire with over 25 years of service to the San Francisco Public Utilities Commission, and introduced Terrance Gardner, Rhonda Tessaro, and Steve W. Thomazin. Terrence Gardner served the City and County of San Francisco as a Stationary Engineer for 45 years, from 1981 to 2026, contributing his skill, professionalism, and dedication to the City’s essential water and wastewater operations. Rhonda Tessaro dedicated 35 years of her life to providing excellent service for the Hetch Hetchy Water Division, for employees of the City and County of San Francisco; and for guests coming to visit the Hetch Hetchy Water & Power System. Steve W. Thomazin dedicated over two decades of service to the Hetch Hetchy Water & Power System, contributing his engineering expertise, professionalism, and commitment to the City and County of San Francisco. Commission Vice President Stacy thanked the incredibly dedicated employees, stated the SFPUC benefitted from their time, and wished all of them the best. President Leveroni stated the SFPUC is grateful to have had these three incredibly great employees for a cumulative period totaling 106 years, expressed excitement for their contributions and mentorship of new employees, and thanked them for all of the years

Update on General Manager Selection Process
items.text: Update on General Manager Selection Process (Discussion only) Vice President Stacy reported that the GM preliminary recruitment period closes on Friday, October 16, 2026; the GM selection process discussion is scheduled for the next CAC meeting and Vice President Stacy will attend to hear thoughts and priorities expressed during that meeting; the BAWSCA policy committee will discuss the GM selection process at their next meeting and Vice President Stacy plans to attend their meeting also; the survey period closed on Friday, October 9, 2026 and the survey results will be shared next week with a total of 236 staff respondents and just under 100 responses from members of the public. Commissioner Arce thanked Vice President Stacy for her work to support this process. Commissioner Jamdar stated she spoke with a group of advocates who expressed concerns regarding the new General Manager selection and intends to share feedback received with the Commission via email
